articles.headline: Bills DB Gardner-Johnson's one-game suspension for spitting stands after appeal
articles.description: Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson's one-game suspension for spitting at Raiders players in Sunday's game has been upheld by hearing officer Jordy Nelson.
articles.headlineJa: ビルズのDBガードナー＝ジョンソン、唾を吐いたことによる1試合の出場停止処分、異議申し立て後も維持
articles.descriptionJa: ビルズのセーフティ、C.J.ガードナー＝ジョンソンが日曜日の試合でレイダースの選手に唾を吐いたことによる1試合の出場停止処分について、審理官のジョーディ・ネルソンは処分を維持すると決定した。
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson's one-game suspension for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders players in Sunday's game has been upheld by appeals hearing officer Jordy Nelson, the league announced Thursday.

Gardner-Johnson is one of two Bills players who were suspended for spitting during the road game against the Raiders. Defensive back and special teams captain Sam Franklin Jr. also was suspended for one game. Franklin denied spitting in a post to his Instagram Story on Wednesday and also has appealed his suspension.

Gardner-Johnson will miss the Bills' Week 8 game against the visiting Baltimore Ravens. Buffalo is on a bye this week.

Bills coach Joe Brady said Monday that there'll be no further punishment for Gardner-Johnson from the team beyond the league's suspension. Brady remained committed to Gardner-Johnson as a starter when he's eligible to return from suspension in Week 9.

Gardner-Johnson was ejected from Sunday's game after spitting in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum shortly before halftime. He apologized to his teammates after the Bills' 33-30 victory and said he needed to be a better veteran moving forward.

ESPN's Nick Suss contributed to this report.

ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Thursday

Thursday's NBA slate features just two games, both between teams with championship aspirations

LeBron James will make his home debut with the Philadelphia 76ers against a Cleveland Cavaliers team led by Donovan Mitchell, James Harden and Evan Mobley. Cleveland added Peyton Watson this offseason but could be without Jarrett Allen, who is questionable for Thursday's game with a knee injury. If Allen can't play, defending Joel Embiid becomes an even bigger challenge. Philadelphia opened the season with a win over the defending champion New York Knicks on Tuesday.

The second game features Nikola Jokic and the Denver Nuggets opening their season on the road against the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Thunder beat the San Antonio Spurs on Tuesday behind 32 points from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. Denver added DeMar DeRozan and Marvin Bagley III this offseason but lost the aforementioned Watson to the Cavs, leaving the Nuggets with a different bench rotation.

Let's take a closer look at both matchups and some fantasy streamers and betting angles worth considering.

Fantasy stream team: Widely available players worth adding

 Aaron Gordon, PF, Nuggets (rostered in 51.6% of ESPN leagues)

Gordon averaged 16.2 PPG and 5.8 RPG in 36 games last season, providing fantasy managers with scoring, rebounds and 3-pointers. He's projected to average 29.3 MPG this season and should see enough minutes to be useful in fantasy. Gordon had 23 points and 10 rebounds in his only game against the Thunder last season.

 Jared McCain, SG/PG, Thunder (43.6%)

McCain finished with 37 fantasy points in 22 minutes against the Spurs on Tuesday. He averaged 10.4 PPG and shot 39.1% from beyond the arc after joining Oklahoma City last season. Don't expect six triples every night, but McCain should continue getting opportunities off the bench.

Moody's favorite bets for Thursday

Tyrese Maxey OVER 2.5 3-pointers (-109)

Maxey played 40 minutes against the Knicks on Tuesday, making just two of his nine 3-point attempts. He averaged 8.6 3-point attempts and 3.1 triples made per game since the 2023-24 season. Maxey should continue playing heavy minutes and has a great chance of making at least three triples tonight against a Cavaliers team that allowed one of the highest totals of 3-pointers made to guards last season.

Anfernee Simons 10+ points (+103)

Simons scored 13 points on 10 field-goal attempts in 25 minutes against the Knicks. The 76ers have several offensive playmakers, but Simons' role is clear. articles.headline: Soccer's main characters after UCL Matchday 3: Kane, Van Dijk, El Clasico
articles.description: Champions League Matchday 3 has come and gone, and we have some Main Character energy coming from Harry Kane, Barcelona and Real Madrid ahead of El Clasico, while Liverpool should worry about Virgil van Dijk's form.
articles.headlineJa: UCL第3節終了後のサッカー界の主役：ケイン、ファン・ダイク、エル・クラシコ
articles.descriptionJa: チャンピオンズリーグ第3節が終了した。エル・クラシコを前にハリー・ケイン、バルセロナ、レアル・マドリードが主役級の存在感を示している一方で、リヴァプールはフィルジル・ファン・ダイクのコンディションを懸念する必要があるだろう。
articles.body:
`

By the time they were going for their third straight Champions League title in 2017-18, Real Madrid had mastered the art of easing in. In 2016-17, they finished behind Borussia Dortmund in their group and constantly needed their trademarked, late-game Real Madrid magic to secure points before igniting in the knockout rounds. For the three-peat, they finished second in their group behind Tottenham Hotspur, but mostly rolled in the spring again.

Paris Saint-Germain have certainly learned that you don't have to look your sharpest early on. Two seasons ago, in their first of what is currently a two-year title streak -- and in the first year for the expanded league phase structure -- they narrowly beat Girona in their first match and then lost three of their next four matches before finally starting to click into place in December. They won their next five Champions League matches by a combined 18 goals, knocked off top-seeded Liverpool in penalties in the round of 16 and ... mostly rolled from there.

You can play with fire without getting burned, but Luis Enrique has decided he really doesn't want to. PSG started far better last year, winning four of their first five league phase matches, and this fall they've been all business: After a 6-1 tuneup against Slovan Bratislava to start, they've beaten Manchester City and Barcelona, each by multiple goals. They were winless in their first four matches in all competitions in this campaign, but when the Champions League began, so did their season.

- UCL Power Rankings: Can anyone slow PSG down?

- Talking Points: Man United's mess, PSG lose Kvara, more

- Dawson: Who are Como, the destination club making waves

Along with a 2-2 draw between Arsenal and Bayern Munich, PSG's 4-2 win over Barcelona was the most noteworthy result of Champions League Matchday 3, even if Khvicha Kvaratskhelia's ACL tear cast a bit of a pall on the proceedings. But five teams continued their perfect starts -- PSG, Real Madrid, Liverpool, Aston Villa and Real Betis -- and all of the most likely candidates to win next week's Ballon d'Or made exciting plays.

The league phase keeps rolling, but here are soccer's five main characters as we move past Matchday 3.

Main character No. 1: Harry Kane's closing argument

The voting for this year's Ballon d'Or, which will be awarded this coming Monday, closed a while ago. While the prediction market odds were shifting toward Barca's Lamine Yamal for a while, they appear to have homed in on Bayern Munich's Harry Kane as the likely winner, and justifiably so. He simply had the best year of anyone, winning three trophies, leading England to the World Cup semifinals for a second time and -- oh yeah -- scoring 73 goals with eight assists in 65 total matches. Yamal had only 25 and 20, respectively, in the same period. articles.headline: Man United players get Thursday day off despite Como thrashing - sources
articles.description: Manchester United's first-team squad will report back for training on Friday after being given a day off on Thursday following the humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat against Como, sources have told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: マン・ユナイテッド、コモに大敗したものの木曜日は休養へ ― 関係者談
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNが報じた関係者の話によると、チャンピオンズリーグでコモに4-1という屈辱的な敗北を喫したマンチェスター・ユナイテッドのトップチームは、木曜日に休日を与えられ、金曜日にトレーニングに復帰する予定だ。
articles.body:
Manchester United's first-team squad will report back for training on Friday after being given a day off today following the humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat against Como, sources have told ESPN.

The result against the Serie A side was United's heaviest Champions League loss since a 4-0 reverse against Barcelona in November 1994 and leaves Michael Carrick's team in 21st position in the League Phase table after one win and two defeats in their opening three games in the competition.

But despite the magnitude of the defeat against Cesc Fàbregas' side, which led to captain Bruno Fernandes criticising the team's tactics -- Carrick responded by questioning the "running" of his players -- sources have said that the players will take their pre-arranged day off today before preparing for Sunday's Premier League home clash with Bournemouth on Friday.

United's flight back from Italy landed at Manchester at 12.20 a.m. on Thursday morning and sources have said that the decision to give the players a day off was based on recovery ahead of the weekend fixture against Bournemouth, who are in Europa League action against AC Milan on Thursday.

United are winless in their last seven games in all competitions and have lost four of those fixtures, against Manchester City, Brighton, Atlético Madrid and Como.

They go into the Bournemouth game sitting 13th in the Premier League having won just one league game all season with fitness concerns over several players including Luke Shaw, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Lisandro Martínez, Ayden Heaven and Benjamin Sesko.

- Tielemans: 'Everything missing' in Utd's Como loss

- Champions League talking points: What to make of the Man Utd mess

- Carragher slams Fernandes for Carrick criticism

"I'm frustrated, more than frustrated. I'm really angry, to be honest," Carrick said after Thursday's game.

"But you've got to move on, you've got to deal with what's next and see what that looks like.

"At this moment in time, there's a lot to do before that next game, to get the team ready, because that was a difficult night for everyone."

articles.headline: Michael Carrick set to lead Man United vs. Bournemouth amid pressure - sources
articles.description: Michael Carrick is set to be in charge of Manchester United against Bournemouth this weekend, sources have told ESPN, as he battles to keep his job at Old Trafford.
articles.body:
Michael Carrick is set to be in charge of Manchester United against Bournemouth this weekend, sources have told ESPN, as he battles to keep his job at Old Trafford.

Carrick is under mounting pressure following the disastrous 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Despite serious concerns internally about the team's form, the 45-year-old is expected to be on the touchline when United face Marco Rose's side on Sunday.

Having only signed a two-year contract in May, Carrick's long-term future remains in doubt after a run of seven games without a win and just one Premier League victory all season.

The club's hierarchy accept that if results do not turn around quickly they will be forced into a change, but there is also sympathy for Carrick's predicament.

Senior staff were left shocked at the team's performance against Como and felt that only Amad Diallo, who was introduced as a half-time substitute, emerged with any credit.

Sources have also told ESPN that there is a feeling that too many players are refusing to take personal responsibility for their own role in the team's slump.

Bruno Fernandes was substituted in the 67th minute at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium before appearing to criticise Carrick and his staff for their tactics in a post-match interview.

- Michael Carrick hits back at Bruno Fernandes criticism after Man United loss

- Man United's worst league starts ever: How does 2026-27 compare?

- Frank Leboeuf blasts Bruno Fernandes for 'betrayal'

The United captain is the second senior player to turn his fire on club staff in as many weeks after Lisandro Martínez directly criticised director of football Jason Wilcox and the board following the 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid.

Martínez later issued a public apology and received a fine. Sources have told ESPN that Fernandes' comments will be assessed before a decision is made about whether to take any further action.

Carrick is set to hold his usual weekly news conference on Friday afternoon to preview Bournemouth's visit to Old Trafford.

United's first-team squad will report back for training on Friday after being given a day off on Thursday, sources have told ESPN.

Information from ESPN's Mark Ogden was used in this report.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

- Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, and Lisandro Martínez are playing for their futures at Old Trafford, with their contracts due to expire next summer. That's according to according to TEAMtalk, which claims that United are not rushing to make a decision on the three defenders. That comes as preparations are being put in place for potential defensive reinforcements in 2027, with center back and left back set to be the main areas of consideration.

- Chelsea are showing interest in a move for Brighton midfielder Yasin Ayari, claims TEAMtalk. The 23-year-old Sweden international is in talks with the Seagulls over a contract extension, with his deal expiring in the summer, though the club has the option to extend it by a further year. However, while there are hopes of sealing a long-term stay with the club, talks have stalled over an improved contract. That has brought Chelsea into the conversation, with the Blues eyeing another swoop on Brighton, while Turkish Super Lig side Galatasaray are also monitoring the situation.

- If Viktor Gyökeres does leave Arsenal in the next year, then the North London club has set a valuation of £55 million on a potential exit, reports Football Insider. That is the same amount as the initial fee the Gunners paid Sporting CP to land the striker last summer. However, after a slow start to the current campaign, the Sweden international continues to be linked with a possible move away. Clubs in Italy, Spain, and elsewhere in England are keeping track of the situation, should the 28-year-old become available.

- Arsenal are among a group of teams following a potential switch for Monza striker Gustavo Varela. That's according to Mundo Deportivo, which claims that the Gunners are joined by Napoli and the 21-year-old's former club, Benfica, in keeping track of his progress. Varela has scored eight goals in seven matches across all competitions for Monza, making an impressive start with his new club. While Benfica is keen on a return, there is no clause that could guarantee a move back to Portugal, though there is a clause that will allow for the club to match an offer accepted from another club. However, with Arsenal and Napoli in the mix, that prospect has been described as difficult.

articles.headline: NFL Week 7 uniforms: Alternates galore as Texans go battle red, Lions all-black
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 7, led by alternate looks from Houston, Detroit and Dallas.
articles.body:
The throwbacks were well-represented in Week 6 of the NFL slate. While that's still the case this week, it's the alternates that lead the way -- including two monochromatic looks from the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions.

Houston will be wearing its "battle red" combination, which the team first unveiled in 2024. It's all red from head to toe complete with a similarly colored matte lid that includes a new bullhorn logo. The numbers are deep steel blue with a liberty white trim, while the red pants boast blue and white stripes. The New York Giants will counter with all-white. 

Also unveiled in 2024, the Lions are rocking their all-black threads against the Green Bay Packers. The black jersey and pants include a Honolulu Blue matte helmet with leaping Lions logo in silver. There's also a black stripe across the middle. Detroit first wore black uniforms in 1948 before bringing it back in 2005 as an alternate. The team stopped wearing them after the 2007 season before returning it in 2024. 

The Dallas Cowboys will don their color rush look against the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football." Dallas unveiled these threads in 2015 with a silver helmet before an arctic white one debuted in 2022. The all-white combination has navy blue numbers and on the shoulder for a neat look.

Though alternates are the headliners, fans of the classics aren't leaving empty handed either in Week 7.

The Seattle Seahawks are wearing their throwbacks from the 1990s, complete with royal blue jerseys and silver pants and helmet. Seattle wore them last week on "Thursday Night Football." For the first time this season, the Atlanta Falcons and New York Jets are rocking classic uniforms. New York's is appropriately named "The Classic," and the all-white look pays homage to the 1968 championship season. It also includes uniform details from 1998 to 2018. Atlanta's threads include its iconic red helmet, which dates back to the 1960s, with black jerseys and white pants.

articles.headline: Mourinho made Real Madrid-Barcelona Clásico rivalry unmissable. Now, he's back for more
articles.description: Thirteen years after helping turn soccer's biggest rivalry into must-see chaos, Real Madrid coach José Mourinho returns to face Barcelona in El Clásico with something to prove
articles.body:
José Mourinho says he doesn't look back. In August, at his debut news conference as returning Real Madrid coach after 13 years away from LaLiga, he was asked if he'd missed the Bernabéu.

"I'm not one for regrets," he said. "I'm not one for [thinking about] bad decisions, missing things ... I'm here today, there tomorrow. I don't think much about what I've left behind."

In El Clásico, club football's most storied rivalry, Mourinho left plenty behind. In three tumultuous seasons in charge of Madrid between 2010 and 2013, he faced Barcelona 17 times in LaLiga, the Copa del Rey, the Spanish Supercopa and the UEFA Champions League.

- Watch El Clásico live, 10/25, 4 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN+ (U.S.)

- Valverde and Güler show why they'll be key for Madrid in El Clásico

- Master of reinvention: How Raphinha transformed into Barça's star striker

For the first two years, his adversary in the Camp Nou dugout was Pep Guardiola; in the third, it was Guardiola's former assistant, Tito Vilanova. By the end, Mourinho's Clásico record read: five wins, six draws, and six defeats.

In that time, both teams delivered unprecedented 100-point seasons, their duelling stars pushing each other to new heights. In 2011-12, Lionel Messi scored a record 50 goals in LaLiga. It wasn't enough to beat Mourinho's Madrid to the title. But numbers alone cannot adequately describe that feverish period.

This was, in many ways, peak Clásico. Pep vs. José. Messi vs. Cristiano Ronaldo. It wasn't always pretty; it was sometimes downright nasty. But it was always riveting. And there, at the centre of it all, revelling in the spotlight, was Mourinho, orchestrating the chaos.

"In this [press] room, he's the f---ing boss, he's the f---ing man," an exasperated Guardiola vented in April 2011. "He's the smartest guy in the world."

Guardiola is long gone, but Mourinho is back, chosen by president Florentino Pérez as the coach to get Madrid on track after two trophyless seasons, and to tame a dressing room which proved too temperamental for predecessors Xabi Alonso and Álvaro Arbeloa to handle. On Sunday, in his first Clásico in 13-and-a-half years, Mourinho has the chance to prove that despite a long absence, he was always the right man for the job.

The panorama he finds now, in 2026, isn't radically different from when Mourinho first took charge at the Bernabéu in May 2010, having just won the Champions League with Inter Milan. Then, as now, Madrid had gone two seasons without any silverware. Then, as now, Mourinho was tasked with besting a Barcelona side which was already well established, supremely confident, and expertly coached.

Guardiola had already been Barça coach for two seasons. In his first, 2009-10, he had won a historic Treble. When Mourinho arrived in the summer of 2010, Guardiola was on the way to lifting a record six trophies in the calendar year.

articles.headline: How Sam Presti's 'slow and steady' trust in SGA created a two-time MVP
articles.description: The Thunder GM and the two-time MVP have created a partnership that fueled OKC's rise.
articles.body:
ONE DAY IN the early stages of their relationship, Thunder general manager Sam Presti asked Shai Gilgeous-Alexander to stop by his office to pick up a book.

"I was expecting some long book, like full of pages and stories and a bunch of chapters and wisdom and stuff like that," Gilgeous-Alexander told ESPN on the eve of his season-opening win over the San Antonio Spurs.

"Have you ever read 'The Tortoise and the Hare'?" Presti asked Gilgeous-Alexander, who was a bit confused by the question.

Surely, Presti couldn't have been referring to the classic childhood fable originally composed by the ancient Greek storyteller Aesop. Gilgeous-Alexander figured there must have been "a real book for, like, grown-ups" with the same title.

No, Gilgeous-Alexander told Presti, he hadn't read that book. Then Presti pulled out a children's book.

"Wait, what? Of course I have," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

Presti proceeded to explain how the moral of the book's story applied to Gilgeous-Alexander's development and the GM's vision for the Thunder's evolution into a contender. The gift was a plea for patience from Presti and a promise to travel a slow, steady path to NBA prosperity together.

"My journey resonates a lot with that," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "It just kind of made sense."

It was a message that particularly applied after Gilgeous-Alexander's second season in Oklahoma City, which was the frustrating first year of Presti's full-blown rebuilding plan.

Gilgeous-Alexander had spent much of that season as a spectator, sitting out the second half of the season because of a lingering case of plantar fasciitis while the Thunder took a cautious approach to his treatment and limped to a 22-50 record and lottery pick. His status as the new face of the franchise in Oklahoma City meant he was toiling in national obscurity.

Meanwhile, a pair of guards selected before him in the 2018 draft class were thriving on playoff teams. Dallas' Luka Doncic was already a two-time first-team All-NBA selection, and Trae Young had been an All-Star and just led the Atlanta Hawks to an Eastern Conference finals appearance. Memphis' Ja Morant, who was taken in the next draft, had just made his playoff debut and also was widely viewed as an ascending superstar.

Gilgeous-Alexander quietly viewed himself as a peer of those other young guards, believing he had just as much potential, a minority opinion at the time but one that Presti shared. Presti reiterated that the Thunder couldn't take shortcuts on the journey to becoming a sustainable contender.

As Presti told Gilgeous-Alexander when he gifted him the children's book, "Slow and steady wins the race."

During the 2021 offseason, Gilgeous-Alexander and Presti agreed to a five-year, $172 million maximum extension of his rookie contract.
